Update, Nov 23: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov 22, and the Nasdaq 100 fund (QQQ) rose about 7% in Monday morning trading. Anthropic traded little changed, at about $89, so it is still about 33 times sales. The figures below are at Friday's close.

Anthropic began trading on Thursday, Nov 19. It sold its shares at $83 and closed its first day at $97.17, up 17.1%. On Friday, Nov 20, it closed at $88.91. That was 8.5% below Thursday's close and still 7.1% above the offer price.

Did Friday's slide make the stock cheap? We looked at what the last ten giant US listings did after a day like Friday.

Did Friday change the multiple? Yes, by about three points. The multiple here is market value divided by sales over the last four quarters. Anthropic booked $35.3 billion of revenue in those four quarters. The final prospectus lists 13.22 billion shares. At Thursday's close, that made Anthropic worth about $1.28 trillion, about 36 times sales. At Friday's $88.91, it is worth about $1.18 trillion, or 33 times.

About $109 billion of market value came off Thursday's close in one trading day. That is about three years of Anthropic's sales at the pace of the last four quarters. Whether 33 times sales holds up depends on how long the growth lasts. We looked at that question in Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Anthropic was not alone. The S&P 500 fund (SPY) fell 2.0% on Thursday and 3.6% on Friday. The Nasdaq-100 fund (QQQ) fell 2.2% and 5.7%. SpaceX, June's giant listing, fell 7.7% on Friday. Anthropic's first buyers paid up just as the market turned down.

At 33 times sales, some investors may want Anthropic at a lower price. Waiting for it means cash set aside for a while. The right price can take months. Meanwhile, the Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3x the S&P 500's, from 50 stocks with at least 10 straight years of dividends. See if it fits.

Is A Second-Day Fall Unusual?

No. Seven of ten fell. We went back to the ten giant US listings in our earlier study, from Google in 2004 to SpaceX in June. We measured each one's second trading day. Seven fell, by 3.8% (Airbnb) to 11.0% (Meta). Reddit fell 8.8%, close to Anthropic's 8.5% on Friday. We compare closes only, so every listing gets the same test. The digital advertising landscape is shifting as data-driven platforms fight for marketing budgets. Choosing between AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) and Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) requires weighing a seasoned software powerhouse against a rapidly growing social platform.

AppLovin specializes in ad-tech software that helps developers grow their apps, while Reddit operates a massive network of user-generated communities. Both companies are successfully capitalizing on specialized data to attract advertisers, but they operate with different business models and cost structures.

The case for AppLovin

AppLovin provides a software-based marketing platform and advertising solutions for consumer brands and gaming apps. The company notes that some of its customers are also competitors, such as Meta Platforms, Alphabet, Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), and Unity Software (NYSE:U). Following the June 2025 divestiture of its Apps business, the company focuses entirely on its high-margin software platform.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $7.6 billion, representing growth of approximately 46.5% compared to the prior period. Net income was roughly $5.0 billion during this time frame, supported by a strong net margin of 65.9%. This performance highlights the company's ability to scale its ad-tech infrastructure efficiently while maintaining significant profitability.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 1.7x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio was 3.3x, a measure of the ability to pay short-term bills using current assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow, which is cash from operations minus capital expenditures, was nearly $3.9 billion.

The case for Reddit

Reddit is establishing itself as a unique player among communication stocks by leveraging its vast array of user-generated communities. The company generates roughly 94% of its revenue from third-party advertisers, though it is expanding into content licensing for AI model training. While it serves a global audience, Reddit faces some customer concentration, with its top ten advertisers accounting for approximately 21% of total revenue.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $3.1 billion, fueled by growth of approximately 62.2%. Net income was close to $991.7 million, marking a significant transition to profitability compared to previous years. The platform continues to focus on increasing user engagement and expanding its data-licensing partnerships to diversify its income streams.

Reddit's latest quarter showed solid revenue and advertising growth, alongside management warnings that search referral traffic is declining faster, which could affect future user activity and the monetization mix.

The company is pushing AI powered ads, shopping tools, and tighter control over third party AI access as it tries to offset weaker search driven traffic with more direct engagement and on platform commerce.

We will examine how Reddit's investment narrative holds up as management confronts accelerating search referral declines and leans harder into AI driven monetization.

Reddit Investment Narrative Recap

To own Reddit, you need to believe the platform can convert deep community intent into durable advertising and commerce revenue even as search referrals fade. According to John_Eric, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, the key upside comes from high gross margins, strong recent earnings growth and a near debt free balance sheet that supports continued product investment.

The near term catalyst now is whether AI driven ads and shopping tools can keep revenue growth resilient while daily users face pressure from weaker Google referrals. The biggest risk is that search driven declines hurt engagement faster than on platform monetization ramps, which could keep volatility and execution scrutiny high.

The most relevant update is Reddit's push into AI powered product discovery and shopping, including tests that surface ads near search style queries and summarize community reviews. This directly targets the referral problem by trying to keep users researching and buying inside Reddit instead of bouncing out to external sites.

If these tools gain traction, they could support ad pricing, attract more retail and B2B marketers and reduce reliance on outside search engines over time. Execution risk is real, especially with RDDT's share price having fallen sharply in recent months and sentiment already cautious, but successful adoption would speak directly to the core traffic and monetization catalyst.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Reddit (RDDT) stock closed at $94.48 on November 17, 2026, down 39.5% from its October 16 close. A drop that steep tempts anyone who liked the company at a higher price. The shares might be a bargain on a business that is still growing. Or they could be a warning that the underlying story has changed. The steepest single-day decline arrived right after Reddit reported its fiscal Q3 2026 results on October 29. So what did management tell investors on that call?

What Did Reddit Tell Investors On Its Q3 Call?

Search referral traffic, the visitors search engines send to Reddit, fell meaningfully in the third quarter, management said on the call. The decline sped up late in the quarter, management said. Management said the slide continued into early October. At that rate, it said, daily users could fall from 130 million by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter. The shares lost 29.2% on October 30, the day after the call. That marked their largest one-day fall of the past year.

Management said on the call that the drop in search traffic appears to come from Google's rollout of AI Mode. It said people still want Reddit, and Google is just not sending them there the way it used to. Management also said 80% of Reddit's monetization happens in its app and among logged-in users. So the search warning on the call was about how many people reach Reddit, not about the ads it has already sold. On the same call, management guided fourth-quarter revenue growth below the third quarter's pace.

Did Reddit's Earlier Falls Of This Size Pay Off?

Since March 2024, Reddit stock has fallen more than 40% over 30 trading days three times. The latest, on November 2, 2026, came partway through this slide. The February 2026 drop is less than a year old. So only one has a full year behind it. In the 30 trading days to March 10, 2025, the shares fell 41.2% while the S&P 500 ETF fell 8.0%. A year after that date, they were 30.0% higher.

Collecting that gain meant sitting through a further fall first. At their lowest that year, the shares closed 19.0% below the March 10 price. The highest price came 192 days after the dip, about six months later. It stood 152.3% above the dip-date price. The February 2026 drop remains too recent to judge over a year, but the shares traded 14.0% higher six months on.

Key Takeaways

Reddit stock is down 57% this year as Google's AI search sends it fewer visitors.

Reddit still guided to about 40% fourth-quarter growth, and free cash flow hit $1.2 billion over 12 months.

Counting stock pay as a cost, the stock trades at about 21x owner's earnings.

That's a fair price for this growth, but Google holds the leverage.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) stock is down 57% this year, closing at $98.45 on Nov. 13. It sank 29% in a day on Oct. 30, after a third-quarter report with 53% revenue growth.

The problem is Alphabet (GOOG): Google's AI answers send fewer people to Reddit. U.S. daily users fell to 50.7 million in the third quarter from 53.2 million in the second, according to Reddit's 10-Q, and management warned total daily users could fall by a low-double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter if referrals keep sliding.

On a recent episode of We Study Billionaires, Shawn O'Malley, who owns the stock, argued the selloff left the stock cheap, stock pay and all:

"Once you strip out the cash and the stock-based comp, you're really paying something like a low 20s multiple of what I would call owner's earnings for a business that is still guiding to 40% growth."

He's mostly right.

Reddit Is Still Growing 40%

Fourth-quarter guidance of $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion means about 40% growth. With U.S. daily users down, more of that growth has to come from earning more per user, and it is: U.S. revenue per daily user rose to $13.82 from $11.85 in the second quarter.

Analysts expect revenue to grow from $2.2 billion last year to $5.38 billion by 2028:

RDDT Revenue, Actual and Consensus Estimates: 2024-2028 (TIKR)

That has growth slowing to 28% in 2027, and the 2027 estimate slipped to $4.35 billion from $4.47 billion in late October.

The Cash Is Real, and So Is the Stock Pay

Reddit went from burning cash to $684 million of free cash flow last year:

RDDT Free Cash Flow: 2021-2025 (TIKR)

Stock-based compensation came to $131 million in the third quarter, 15% of revenue (shareholder letter). Grieve treats it as a real cost. Free cash flow reached $1.2 billion over the 12 months to Sept. 30, and subtracting about $386 million of stock-based compensation leaves roughly $812 million of owner's earnings. Buybacks are offsetting the dilution for now.

Key Takeaways

Reddit shares fell 29% on October 30 after the company warned Google's AI search was cutting referral traffic, even though revenue jumped 53% to $895 million.

CEO Steve Huffman said "the AI mode does not drive traffic," and US daily users fell 2% to 50.7 million, the first decline since the IPO.

Pinterest also sank on a weak forecast, while Reddit's fourth-quarter guide of $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion implies growth slowing to 38% to 42%.

The fourth-quarter report, expected in February, will show how far daily users fell and whether logged-in tests keep people engaged.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) just posted one of the strongest quarters in social media. Revenue jumped 53% to $895 million, and net income rose 74% to $283 million.

Investors sold anyway. The culprit is Alphabet (GOOGL:NASDAQ), whose AI Overviews and AI Mode now answer questions before anyone clicks through to a Reddit thread. Pinterest (PINS:NYSE) sank the same morning after forecasting fourth-quarter revenue of $1.425 billion to $1.475 billion, below Wall Street estimates.

Reddit fell 29% on October 30, its biggest one-day drop since the IPO. That also left the stock at its lowest level in more than a year.

Both names were already weak in 2026. Reddit had fallen about 44% before its report, while Pinterest was down about 23%.

A blowout quarter with a crack

Reddit's third quarter beat on nearly every financial line:

Revenue rose 53% to $895 million, with advertising up 54% to $847 million.

Diluted EPS reached $1.40, ahead of the $1.35 analysts expected.

Free cash flow nearly doubled to $363 million, a 41% margin.

Growth is cooling, though. Revenue rose 61% in the second quarter. The fourth-quarter guide of $1.00 billion to $1.03 billion implies just 38% to 42%.

Here is how close Reddit is getting to a $1 billion quarter…

Reddit (RDDT): total revenue, quarterly, actual and consensus estimate, $ millions, Q3 2024–Q4 2026 (TIKR)

Even the low end of guidance would put it above that line for the first time.

The user numbers told a different story. Daily active uniques reached 130.3 million, short of the 133.7 million analysts expected. In the US, they fell 2% to 50.7 million, the first decline since the IPO.

Google holds the front door

Search referrals dropped by more than 1 million a week on average in October. CEO Steve Huffman was blunt about why, saying on the earnings call that "the AI mode does not drive traffic, not for us and not to anybody."

So how has the market treated Reddit against its gatekeeper and its closest ad peer?

Reddit (RDDT) stock has lost 52.2% over the past twelve months, while the S&P 500 returned 12.2%. The shares now sit 61.6% below their January 2026 high, and on the October 29 call management warned that the number of people using Reddit each day could fall in the final quarter of 2026. Is $99.55 a low enough price to buy before Reddit shows whether it actually loses users?

Reddit Costs Less Than The S&P 500 On Earnings

Reddit trades at 19.3 times its earnings over the last twelve months, against 21.9 for the S&P 500. On sales the multiple has fallen sharply: buyers paid 22.7 times sales at the end of September 2025, and they pay 6.2 times today, still above the 3.2 for the S&P 500. That cheaper price comes with better margins, not worse ones. Reddit's operating margin over the twelve months to September 2026 was 29.4%, its highest at any of the 21 quarter ends since September 2021.

Profit is taxed lightly for now, with a tax rate of about 2% in the third quarter. That low rate lifts reported profit, so the earnings multiple would be higher at a normal tax rate. On cash, Reddit trades at 15.9 times operating cash flow, about level with 15.4 for the S&P 500, so on both measures Reddit is priced close to the market or below it.

The business kept growing, too: revenue rose 53% in the third quarter. Management's caution on the call was about users. Management said search referral traffic fell meaningfully in the quarter, with the decline speeding up late, and that Google is not sending people to Reddit the way it used to.

What Must Reddit Deliver In Its Fourth Quarter?

Reddit has guided fourth-quarter revenue of $1.0 billion to $1.03 billion, or 38% to 42% above a year earlier. The consensus for that quarter is $1.05 billion. With that figure sitting about $20 million above the top of the guide, the price appears to assume another beat. That sets a high bar for a company whose growth slowed in each quarter of 2026, dropping from 69.1% in the first to 53.0% in the third.

Management also warned about users. Search traffic dropped by more than 1 million referrals a week on average in October. If that pace continues, management said, daily users could fall in the fourth quarter by a low double-digit percentage from 130 million. Reddit will also begin testing a logged-in-only version in select markets outside the U.S. in the same quarter, which management said will likely trade reach for engagement.
